Subject guide

Live cooking programs and culinary workshops

Learn cooking techniques with a provider you can ask questions. Choose a program based on the dishes you want to make, your experience, and the equipment you have.

Explore current programs↗

Choose a useful starting point

You might want to understand a cuisine, practise a specific technique, or feel more comfortable preparing a complete meal. Read the outcomes rather than relying on an appealing dish name. Check whether you will cook along, watch a demonstration, or take part in another kind of session.

Think about where you will cook

For a live online program, compare the equipment and ingredients with what you have at home. For an in-person workshop, check the venue details and what you are expected to bring. A program that fits your kitchen and your experience is easier to prepare for than one that assumes tools you have never used.

Ask about ingredients before booking

Look for an ingredient or materials list and raise questions about substitutions, dietary needs, or allergies directly with the provider. The description may not cover every individual requirement. Get the information you need before deciding whether a program is suitable.

Make the practice part realistic

A short workshop can introduce a dish or technique. A program may give you several sessions to build on it. Check the schedule, preparation time, and any work expected between programs. Afterward, use shared resources where the provider provides them and keep follow-up questions with the program discussion.

Before you choose

A few things to check

  • Ingredients and equipment
  • Cook-along or demonstration
  • Dietary questions to ask
  • Preparation before program

Current programs, prices, and dates are available in the app.

Choosing your program

Good questions
to ask.

Are ingredients included?

That depends on the program. Read its materials and requirements, and ask the provider if ingredient costs or preparation are not explained.

Can a provider adapt recipes for me?

Ask before booking. Substitutions and dietary accommodations depend on the recipe, format, and provider. Do not assume that a program can meet a specific dietary need.
